response.message: We'll build a read-only Google Cloud drift and correction advisor. It reads a synthetic inventory, runs policy checks, drafts a correction plan and a reviewable diff, then waits for a person to approve it, with every step logged. It never applies changes, deletes resources or widens its own access. For the first local test, we feed a fixed synthetic inventory with one known drift through the pipeline and check three things: the policy violation is found, a diff is produced, and nothing runs without approval. In that test the model's answers are scripted, so it only shows the wiring works. It doesn't show that Gemini on Vertex AI writes correct plans; that needs a separate evaluation against a real model in an approved project and region, and neither of those is confirmed yet. Which country must the inventory and audit data stay in?

proposal.title: GCP read-only drift analysis and correction-plan pipeline
proposal.body: First concrete sketch on Google Cloud. Scope: synthetic inventory only, with read-only analysis, policy checks, drift detection, plan and diff generation, human approval and audit. Excluded: applying, deleting or escalating credentials. Assumptions: region, project and model access are not selected or verified. Model behaviour is mocked locally. No native Terraform generator exists for this workload yet, so it needs engineering.

data.label: Platform engineer (reviewer)
data.description: Existing person outside the provisioning scope. Starts analysis runs, reviews diffs and records approve/reject decisions. Never triggers an apply through this system.

data.label: Synthetic inventory snapshot
data.description: Private bucket holding synthetic Cloud Asset Inventory-style JSON exports and the declared desired state. Analyzer service account has read-only object viewer access. Real Cloud Asset Inventory reads are a later, separately approved step.

data.label: Inventory & drift analyzer
data.description: Normalizes the inventory, compares it with the desired state and emits drift findings. Runs as a dedicated read-only service account with no write, delete or IAM-admin roles.

data.label: Policy checks
data.description: Deterministic policy evaluation of findings and later of the proposed plan. It rejects any plan containing deletes, apply steps or credential/IAM broadening. The ruleset is versioned.

data.label: Correction plan generator
data.description: Drafts a minimal Terraform-style correction for policy-confirmed drift. Inventory text is treated as untrusted input. Locally the model is scripted; real model quality, regional availability and quotas are unverified.

data.label: Reviewable diff & plan artifacts
data.description: Stores the plan, human-readable diff, findings and policy results per run, immutably versioned. Nothing is applied from here.

data.label: Approval gate
data.description: Records the reviewer's approve/reject decision against a specific diff hash. Approval only marks the plan as reviewed; it does not execute anything.

data.label: Audit trail
data.description: Append-only record of runs, findings, policy verdicts, model calls and approvals for traceability.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If the system could mutate or escalate, a wrong model output could damage infrastructure.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Never apply, delete resources or request broader credentials automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the system must never apply changes, delete resources or request broader credentials. Every identity it uses is read-only, and approval only records a decision.

requirementDrafts.rationale: This is the first observable acceptance test. Mocked model output proves the wiring, not plan quality.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: for a synthetic inventory with known drift, the system must report that drift and produce a policy-checked, reviewable diff.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without this, nobody can trace who approved which plan.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: every run, policy verdict, model call and approval decision is recorded in an append-only audit trail linked to the diff hash. Retention is still to be confirmed.

Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with what the evidence shows is working, explain the most important remaining issue in plain language, and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: The good news is that the design itself holds up. The run has no failures, and every component and connection checked out, including the read-only boundary, the policy re-check loop and the approval-before-anything rule. The run is blocked, though: none of the eight components has a matching Google Cloud implementation in the generator yet. The only Google Cloud one it supports is private object storage, and narrowing the design to that would drop the analyzer, policy checks, Gemini planner, approval and audit. So I'm not changing the board. This is product engineering work: the generator needs native Cloud Run job, OPA policy, Vertex AI, Firestore approval and logging-sink contracts. This report (artifact a03fd3f2…, revision 2) can be the test case, and the emulation should be rerun once those exist. The scripted model responses still say nothing about real Gemini plan quality. While that gets built, we can settle a decision that's yours to make: which country must the inventory, diff and audit data stay in?
